CRF - Stellantis | University of Trento\
Ministero Italiano dello Sviluppo Economico - 2022 - 2024

## Overview

VeDi 2025 is an Italian Ministry of Economic Development (MISE) funded
research project between Centro Ricerche Fiat (CRF, Stellantis) and the
University of Trento, evaluating motion planning approaches in a real
Stellantis test vehicle. It uses V2X (vehicle-to-vehicle and
vehicle-to-infrastructure) communication enabled by the roadside
infrastructure installed on the Brennero highway, and also covers
deploying neural networks directly on the car's experimental ECU. Part of
the work is directly tied to my PhD.

## Two planners

Stellantis wanted two independent planners evaluated in the same vehicle
architecture:

- **CODRIVER** - an existing planner developed by Prof. Mauro Da Lio and
  collaborators during the European project DREAM4CARS, adapted by UniTN
  for this use case.
- **MPTree** - a sampling-based planner built from scratch by me, under
  the supervision of Prof. Francesco Biral. It is derived from RRT*, but
  exploits prior knowledge of the road geometry to shrink the exploration
  domain and reach real-time performance - not standard practice for
  RRT-based planning in robotics - and connects nodes with optimal motion
  primitives and clothoids instead of straight lines.

## Development path

1. MATLAB MVP to validate the core planning approach.
2. The MVP grew into the [VehiclePrimitives](vehicle-primitives.qmd)
   library.
3. C++ port, tested standalone and integrated with the commercial
   simulator IPG CarMaker.
4. SIL and HIL testing on an experimental ECU (dSPACE AUTERA) replaying
   real car logs.
5. VIL testing in the real vehicle, at the Vadena safety test site and at
   Stellantis's Balocco proving ground.

## Maneuver negotiation

Alongside single-vehicle planning, the project required decentralized
negotiation between agents. Vehicles exchange over V2X not just their
current state but their currently committed maneuver, so two vehicles can
plan an intersection crossing, overtake, or cut-in jointly rather than
reactively. A vehicle can also broadcast a *desired* maneuver that differs
from its committed one; the receiving agent folds this into its own tree
search, biasing both expansion and cost function toward a maneuver that
works for both. The scheme is decentralized and emergent, based on mutual
penalization and biasing rather than a central negotiator.

## Publication

*MPTree: A Sampling-based Vehicle Motion Planner for Real-time Obstacle
Avoidance* (IFAC-PapersOnLine, 2024) - also covered in a chapter of my PhD
thesis.

## Status

Completed, 2022 - 2024, developed jointly with CRF - Stellantis at the
University of Trento.
